properties.Notes: ASRR uses special residential lot-size rules that are not fully captured by a single minimum lot-size field. Under Section 252, new residential lots are generally required to be either between 0.5 and 2 acres or at least 25 acres, while residential subdivision density remains limited to 1 dwelling unit per 10 acres. Frontage is also tiered by lot size under Section 211, so the frontage field should be interpreted as simplified. Accessory dwellings are permitted, but they require an owner-occupied detached single-family home, are limited to one bedroom, may be located within or ancillary to the home or in a detached accessory building, and require parking room for at least 3 vehicles on the property. More than 4 lots in this district triggers PUD review, and new residential lots and building envelopes must be configured to protect farmland and reduce fragmentation.

The Flood Hazard Overlay District is an overlay that supplements or supersedes the underlying zoning district rather than functioning as a standard standalone base district. Uses and development are governed by Figure 7 in Section 282, with different standards inside and outside the floodway. New structures are conditional outside the floodway and prohibited within the floodway, while certain improvements, parking, ponds, and small accessory structures are treated differently depending on location. Standard housing-use fields in this row should therefore be interpreted as non-applicable or subordinate to the underlying base district and the flood overlay use table.

Single-family homes and accessory dwellings are not by-right uses in FC; they require reviewed approval under the use table. Accessory dwellings in this district are allowed only within or ancillary to an existing detached single-family home and must satisfy the owner-occupancy, size, bedroom, and parking standards in Section 340. More than 2 lots triggers PUD review, but Starksboro’s PUD standards do not allow the actual developed portion of a PUD to be located within FC; instead, FC land may contribute density transfer and/or open space to a PUD located in another district. This district is also intended to minimize forest fragmentation and requires special attention to road access, habitat protection, and municipal service impacts.

HDRC is the village-centered district and allows the broadest mix of residential, civic, and commercial uses, but multifamily housing is still a reviewed use rather than plain by-right housing under the use table. Residential density is 2 dwelling units per acre, residential lot size is 1 acre minimum, and the road setback is 50 feet from the road centerline with 10-foot residential side and rear setbacks. The bylaw does not impose a maximum residential lot-coverage percentage in HDRC, so any flat impervious-coverage field should be treated as not applicable. PUDs are allowed in HDRC, but unlike other districts they do not need to conserve undeveloped open space; instead they must provide common outdoor space of at least 4,000 square feet or 400 square feet per dwelling, whichever is greater. Accessory dwellings are permitted and follow the general Section 340 standards.

LDRC is a mixed-use district but is primarily residential in emphasis, with care required because much of it is accessed by Class 3 dirt roads. Residential density is 1 dwelling unit per 5 acres, residential lot size is 1 acre minimum, and residential lot coverage is capped at 20%. Frontage is tiered by lot size under Section 211, so a single frontage number is only a simplified representation. PUDs are allowed, and subdivision into more than 4 lots triggers PUD review. Accessory dwellings are permitted and follow the owner-occupancy, size, bedroom, location, and parking rules in Section 340.

MDRC is intended to support appropriately scaled residential and economic development near the traditional centers. Residential density is 1 dwelling unit per 2.5 acres, which means any minimum-lot-size fields for duplexes and multifamily buildings should be derived from that density rather than copied from the 1-acre residential lot-size minimum. Frontage is tiered by lot size under Section 211 and should be treated as simplified in a flat field structure. PUDs are allowed, and subdivision into more than 4 lots triggers PUD review. Accessory dwellings are permitted under Section 340, while multifamily dwellings are reviewed uses rather than plain by-right housing.

WP is not a normal rural residential district. It is a public-water-supply protection district in which land development is strictly limited, and even uses that are otherwise listed in the general use table are only allowed to the extent they do not threaten water quality. Single-family homes, two-family homes, and accessory dwellings are reviewed uses rather than by-right uses in this district. Residential density is 1 dwelling unit per 25 acres, residential lot size is 25 acres minimum, and frontage is tiered by lot size with a 500-foot minimum for large lots. In addition, the bylaw specifically prohibits uses involving fuels, hazardous materials, pesticides, herbicides, repair garages, contractors’ yards, junkyards, landfills, recycling centers, commercial composting, and similar contamination risks. Accessory dwellings also remain subject to the owner-occupancy, size, bedroom, and parking rules in Section 340.
